scenes.tts: Two children have malformed cortices. One is small, with its layers in order. The other is thick and nearly smooth. Which step failed in each?
scenes.visual: Title card: Size Counts the Doublings. Two schematic coronal brain outlines side by side: a small brain with a thin, orderly cortical ribbon, and a normal-sized brain with a thick, smooth cortex.
scenes.narration: Two children have malformed cortices. One is small, with its layers in order. The other is thick and nearly smooth. Which step failed in each?

scenes.tts: Building a cortex takes two jobs. Radial glia at the ventricle divide, to make more of themselves and then neurons.
scenes.visual: The developing cortical wall: radial glia at the ventricle at the bottom, their fibres running up to the surface. Label: job 1, make the neurons.
scenes.narration: Building a cortex takes two jobs. Radial glia at the ventricle divide, to make more of themselves and then neurons.

scenes.tts: Then each neuron climbs a glial fiber to its layer. So too few can be made, or they can stall.
scenes.visual: Newborn neurons climb the fibres. Label: job 2, move them. Two failure cards appear: too few made; made but misplaced.
scenes.narration: Then each neuron climbs a glial fiber to its layer. So too few can be made, or they can stall.

scenes.tts: The first job multiplies. Early on, each division makes two progenitors. So every round doubles the pool.
scenes.visual: A doubling tree grows round by round from one progenitor; a counter shows the pool.
scenes.narration: The first job multiplies. Early on, each division makes two progenitors. So every round doubles the pool.

scenes.tts: Switch one round early, and the pool is halved. Switch two rounds early, and it falls to a quarter.
scenes.caption: Switch one round early, and the pool is halved. Switch two rounds early, and it falls to a quarter.
scenes.visual: Counter from 100 to 12,800 over seven rounds. A table builds: 7 rounds, 12,800, 1; 6 rounds, 6,400, one half; 5 rounds, 3,200, one quarter.
scenes.narration: Switch one round early, and the pool is halved. Switch two rounds early, and it falls to a quarter.

scenes.tts: Now a subtler fault. Suppose each division has a one in ten chance of coming out neurogenic, for that round only.
scenes.visual: In the tree, about one division in ten turns amber at random: one progenitor plus one neuron instead of two progenitors; next round that progenitor divides symmetrically again. Label: illustrative model, one round at a time (a permanent switch would cost more).
scenes.narration: Now a subtler fault. Suppose each division has a one in ten chance of coming out neurogenic, for that round only.

scenes.tts: Predict. Let the pool run ten rounds. How big is it then, compared with normal?
scenes.visual: Question card: each division has a one-in-ten chance of coming out neurogenic, for that round only. Run ten rounds (longer than the table's seven). How big is the pool? Choices: about 90 percent, about 60 percent, about 10 percent.
scenes.narration: Predict. Let the pool run ten rounds. How big is it then, compared with normal?

scenes.tts: About sixty percent. Each neurogenic division is one progenitor short. So each round falls five percent short of doubling.
scenes.caption: About 60 percent. Each neurogenic division is one progenitor short. So each round falls 5 percent short of doubling.
scenes.visual: On screen: on average 1.9 progenitors per division, so 0.95 of normal per round; 0.95 to the tenth power is about 0.60. A bar shrinks to 60 percent.
scenes.narration: About 60 percent. Each neurogenic division is one progenitor short. So each round falls 5 percent short of doubling.

scenes.tts: Over ten rounds, that costs two fifths of the pool. Small faults compound.
scenes.caption: Over ten rounds, that costs two-fifths of the pool. Small faults compound.
scenes.visual: The bar keeps shrinking as more rounds are added. Label: small faults compound.
scenes.narration: Over ten rounds, that costs two-fifths of the pool. Small faults compound.

scenes.tts: The second job does not multiply. A neuron that stalls takes no descendants with it.
scenes.visual: A single neuron stops partway up a fibre; no tree branches from it.
scenes.narration: The second job does not multiply. A neuron that stalls takes no descendants with it.

scenes.tts: At the bedside, size is read with a tape measure. The cutoff for microcephaly is two standard deviations below the mean.
scenes.visual: A tape measure around an infant head, from just above the eyebrows and ears to the back of the head. A scale marks minus 2 SD, the WHO cutoff.
scenes.narration: At the bedside, size is read with a tape measure. The cutoff for microcephaly is two standard deviations below the mean.

scenes.tts: On a rough sphere model, a head at the cutoff holds a brain only about a fifth smaller. That compares volumes. It does not count neurons, or lost divisions.
scenes.visual: The scale fills in: minus 2 SD, volume about 0.80, about a third of one halving; minus 3 SD, about 0.72, about half of one; volume halved, about minus 6 SD. Column label: model volume halvings, not counted divisions. Footnote: rough sphere model, mean 34.5 cm, SD about 1.2 cm.
scenes.narration: On a rough sphere model, a head at the cutoff holds a brain only about a fifth smaller. That compares volumes. It does not count neurons, or lost divisions.

scenes.tts: Children with A S P M mutations often have far smaller heads, many standard deviations below the mean.
scenes.caption: Children with ASPM mutations often have far smaller heads, many standard deviations below the mean.
scenes.visual: A marker far out on the low tail, labelled ASPM families: often many SD below the mean for age. No newborn scale and no round count.
scenes.narration: Children with ASPM mutations often have far smaller heads, many standard deviations below the mean.

scenes.tts: In a bell-shaped population, about two babies in a hundred fall below the cutoff. A small head is a sign, not a diagnosis.
scenes.visual: An ideal bell curve of head sizes, labelled ideal bell-shaped reference population, with the tail below minus 2 SD shaded: about 2 in 100, some of them healthy.
scenes.narration: In a bell-shaped population, about two babies in a hundred fall below the cutoff. A small head is a sign, not a diagnosis.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Size counts the doublings. Layering records the journey.
scenes.visual: Card: Size counts the doublings; layering records the journey.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Size counts the doublings. Layering records the journey.

scenes.tts: Small with orderly layers points to production. Near-normal size with disordered layers points to migration.
scenes.visual: The two brain outlines return, tagged: production; migration.
scenes.narration: Small with orderly layers points to production. Near-normal size with disordered layers points to migration.

scenes.tts: It is a first question, not a diagnosis.
scenes.visual: Small note under the card: a first question, not a diagnosis. Covers making and placing neurons; not tissue destruction, folding or wiring. Some genes act at both steps, and Zika also destroys tissue (collected later in the lesson).
scenes.narration: It is a first question, not a diagnosis.

scenes.tts: So when a cortex is malformed as it is built, ask first which job failed.
scenes.visual: Closing card with two columns: too few made; made but misplaced.
scenes.narration: So when a cortex is malformed as it is built, ask first which job failed.
